pairing.intro: Your music lives on a computer of yours running the Chordia library server. Pairing lets this phone reach it: songs stream straight from that machine and never pass through Chordia.

pairing.stepLinkBody: It looks like https://192.168.1.20:8443/setup/abc123. Copy the whole line, including the code at the end.
pairing.linkInvalid: That is not a setup link. It ends in /setup/ followed by the one-time code the server printed.
pairing.trustBody: {host} signed its own certificate, which is normal for a home server. From now on this phone accepts only this exact certificate and refuses anything else, which is what makes a self-signed server safe to stream from.
pairing.claimingBody: Chordia is issuing a one-time pass, good for two minutes and for nothing but this handshake, and handing it to the server. Your sign-in never leaves this phone.
pairing.ticketExpired: The one-time pass ran out before the server answered. Nothing was lost; try again.
pairing.nameBody: One server can hold several libraries. This is the name you will see on this phone.
pairing.doneBody: The server is scanning its folders now. Tracks appear as they are indexed.
pairing.unreachable: Could not reach {host}. Check the server is running and that this phone is on the same network.
pairing.refused: The server would not accept that setup link. A link works once; restart the library server to print a fresh one.

download.title: Chordia on your desktop
download.subtitle: The same app in its own window. It answers the media keys on your keyboard, keeps your offline downloads on disk, and can play local files without a server at all.
download.unavailable: The list of builds could not be loaded just now. Every release is here:
download.smartScreen: On first run Windows will say it does not recognize the app. The installer is not signed yet, so that warning is expected. Choose More info, then Run anyway.
download.updates: It updates itself from then on, so you should only need this page once.
download.checksums: Want to check what you downloaded?
download.browserBody: Nothing here is desktop only. The web app plays the same library and works offline once you install it from your browser. The desktop build adds the media keys, a window of its own, and local files.

cost.a: Playing your own music is free and always will be; charging you to listen to files you own would be absurd. The software is AGPL-3.0 and all of it is on GitHub. Two paid tiers, Sonic and Super-Sonic, add extras on top for people who want them, and nothing that is free today has moved behind them. Self-hosting stays complete rather than becoming a crippled community edition. See the pricing page for what they cost.

formats.a: FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF, MP3, AAC, Ogg and Opus. Dolby Atmos and other spatial mixes pass through untouched, because re-encoding something we cannot improve helps nobody.

offline.a: Yes. Download an album and it plays with no signal and no server. The files live on the device, not in a stream you have to keep alive.
offline.q: Does it work on a plane?

privacy.a: Your audio never reaches our servers, not even as a cache. Your phone talks straight to your library over an encrypted connection. We hold your account, your friends list and your play history, and you can export or delete all of it whenever you like.

server.a: Your files need somewhere to live: an old laptop, a NAS, a Raspberry Pi, or a cheap VPS. The library server runs on all of them. Point it at a folder and it takes it from there.

spotify.a: Not quite. Chordia plays the music you already have rather than a catalog you rent. Bring the albums you bought, your Bandcamp downloads, your Qobuz purchases. If a folder of files is your idea of a record collection, you are in the right place.

everywhere.body: Chordia runs in the browser on any machine you sign in on, and installs to your home screen on a phone. Gapless playback, crossfade and an equalizer that remembers what you did to it.

points.a: Pick up on your phone exactly where the desktop left off.
points.b: Download an album for the flight and play it with no signal.
points.c: Volume levelled across albums so nothing blows your ears off.

everywhere.title: Everywhere you sign in

features.heading: What you get

quality.body: Original quality is a byte-for-byte stream with no transcode step and no silent downgrade. On a train with two bars Chordia steps down to protect your data, tells you it has, and steps back up when the signal returns.

points.a: FLAC, ALAC and WAV streamed exactly as they are on disk.
points.b: Atmos and other spatial mixes pass through untouched.
points.c: You decide whether it's ever allowed to drop quality.

quality.title: Full quality, or nothing quietly changed

sharing.body: Split your collection into as many libraries as you like, then hand each one to exactly the friends you choose. They browse and stream it like it was always theirs. You can see what they played, and you can take it back in one click.

points.b: Friends stream from your server without an account on it.
points.c: Revoke any time. Access expires on its own too.

sharing.title: Share a shelf, not the whole collection

features.subheading: Four things that are hard to get anywhere else.

yours.body: Chordia never uploads your library, never re-encodes it behind your back, and never holds it hostage. Your library server hands audio straight to your devices. We only ever handle the metadata needed to sign you in and keep your friends list straight.

points.a: Audio goes device to library, never through us.
points.b: Stop using Chordia and every file is where you left it.
points.c: AGPL-3.0. The code we run is the code you get.

yours.title: Your files stay your files

final.body: Make an account, point Chordia at your music, and have it on your phone before the kettle boils.
final.title: Bring your music with you

footer.rights: Chordia is free software, released under the AGPL-3.0.
footer.tagline: Music you own, everywhere you are.

hero.subtitle: Chordia streams the music you already own. The albums you bought, the Bandcamp downloads, the folder you have dragged across three laptops. It goes from wherever you keep it straight to your devices, at full quality, and none of it passes through us.
hero.title: Your library, on every device you own

cancel.a: In Settings, under Plan. It takes one click and there is nothing to email anybody about. You keep the paid features until the end of the period you have already paid for, then the account goes back to free. Nothing is deleted and no music is lost.

free.q: What do I get without paying?
free.a: All of it, for listening. Streaming your own library at full quality, on every device, with playlists, offline downloads, sharing with friends and two years of listening history. Playing music you already own is free and stays free. The paid tiers add appearance and depth on top of that; they do not put anything you can do today behind a payment.

refund.q: What if I change my mind?
refund.a: Email us within 14 days of a charge and we will refund it, no questions asked. That applies to renewals too, not only your first payment.

selfhost.q: What if I run Chordia myself?
selfhost.a: Then none of this applies to you. The software is AGPL-3.0 and self-hosting gives you the complete thing, not a reduced community edition. These plans are for the account on the Hub we host, which is what costs us money to run.

trial.q: How does the free trial work?
trial.a: Every paid plan starts with 7 days free. You get the full tier immediately, and if you cancel before the trial ends you are not charged at all.

pricing.support: Questions about billing, or anything else:
pricing.subtitle: Chordia plays the music you already own, and that part is free. Sonic and Super-Sonic are extras on the account we host for you: how the app looks, how far back your listening history goes, and what you can do with that history.
pricing.terms: Prices in US dollars. Every paid plan starts with 7 days free and can be canceled in one click from Settings. Refunds within 14 days of any charge, no questions asked. Payments are handled by Creem, our merchant of record, who appear on your statement and issue your receipt.
pricing.title: Free to listen. Paid if you want more of it.

about.early_bird: For accounts that were here before this instance opened its doors properly: the first pressing, in record terms.
about.early_supporter: One of the first hundred people to ever pay for Chordia. The number never changes hands.
about.sonic: A current Sonic subscriber. The streak counts unbroken months.

earn.developer: Granted by an admin to people who work on Chordia itself.
earn.staff: Granted by an admin to people who help run this instance.
earn.early_bird: Have an account created before this instance's cutoff date. There is nothing to sign up for; if you were here, you have it.
earn.early_supporter: Be one of the first hundred accounts to ever start a paid subscription. Ranks are never reissued, so a rank that is taken is taken forever.
earn.sonic: Subscribe to Sonic. The badge lasts as long as the subscription does.
earn.super_sonic: Subscribe to Super-Sonic. The badge gains a ring at three, six and twelve unbroken months.
earn.translator: Translate Chordia and ask an admin to add it. The catalogs are community work and there was no way to say so.

noHistory.tooFew: Nobody has earned this yet, so there is nothing to plot.
noHistory.untracked: Not plotted. A subscription badge records when its holder's current streak began, which moves if they lapse and come back, so past totals cannot be recovered. Drawing a line here would mean inventing one.
